topics.label: Lecture Introduction and Learning Objectives
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer introduces the cancer lecture series, outlines the core learning objectives, and sets out the central question of what causes malignancy.

topics.label: Biological Drivers of Cancer and Mutation Sources
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the fundamental nature of cancer as a micro-evolutionary genetic disease driven by mutations from endogenous cellular processes, environmental agents, and inherited traits.

topics.label: Environmental Exposures and Epidemiological Evidence
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine real-world environmental exposures, evaluate the debate between intrinsic bad luck and preventable external factors, and review epidemiological evidence showing global variations in cancer incidence.

topics.label: Pathogen-Driven Carcinogenesis and Burkitt Lymphoma
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how various infectious pathogens drive oncogenesis and examine Burkitt lymphoma as a primary model of infection-associated cancer development.

topics.label: Molecular Mechanisms of Chemical and Physical Mutagenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail how specific chemical carcinogens and UV radiation induce DNA damage either directly or following metabolic activation into reactive intermediates.

topics.label: Tumor Promotion, Multi-Stage Carcinogenesis, and Host Susceptibility
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore non-mutagenic tumor promotion through chronic inflammation and intracellular signaling, the classical multi-stage model of carcinogenesis, and how host developmental stages influence cancer risk.

topics.label: Methodologies for Testing Carcinogenicity and Risk Evaluation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine the genomic, epidemiological, animal, and in vitro methods used to identify carcinogens and assess the practical balance of risks and benefits.
